transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-07
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: 54 min
- Recording: enabled
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood SE), Markus, Priya, Ethan, Sana (SynthEx)

Summary:
Jordan: quick tour of Console request lifecycle, tracing, fallback behavior, and error analysis. Show how we surface KV cache misses, prefix caching, and model fallbacks when Dedicated capacity is tight. Walkthrough includes live demo of a failed request, trace correlation to infra, and steps for debugging.

Topics covered:
- Request trace map and timeline
- Prefix/KV cache hits vs misses and how that impacts latency and cost
- Model variant fallbacks (e.g., small -> standard -> high-accuracy)
- Correlating request ids to infra logs and GPU metrics
- Security and compliance notes (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps: pilot benchmark, security deep dive, share docs

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through the console lifecycle trace and then show how you can drill into errors and fallback behavior, Lina's gonna drive the demo.
00:12 Markus: hey thanks Jordan, quick - we mostly wanna see how an error in inference surfaces across your stack and how fast our SRE can root cause it. we've had late night fires with model timeouts so that's the core.
00:25 Lina: yeah totally, that's what we built the inspector for. i'll start with a synthetic request that times out and then show how we map it back to the serving runtime and the node-level logs. bear with me while i pull up the request inspector.
00:40 Omar: also i'll highlight the cache signals — a lot of teams think caching is a black box, we'll show the hit/miss heatmap.
00:51 Priya: quick infra context - we run on a hybrid cloud, some requests hit on-prem gpus, some on our reserved cloud pool, and we need to ensure data never leaves our VPC. how does that show up?
01:07 Jordan: good point. for Private deployments we provide a control plane that keeps telemetry inside customer VPCs or the telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM. we'll show the VPC flag in the trace metadata.
01:20 Lina: ok pulling up the console. here is the request timeline — at the top we have the user request id, a short summary, and then the timeline bar that shows routing, queue, model execution, and any fallbacks. see here — this request incurred a model fallback.
01:40 Lina: the trace map shows three spans — api gateway, routing/queue, and model exec. the model exec node shows 2.8s but there's a later fallback span where it retried with a smaller variant at 4.7s. that's why overall latency ballooned to ~7.5s.
01:59 Markus: wait so it retried automatically? what triggers the fallback — is it latency SLO, OOM, or a hard failure?
02:10 Lina: good q. policy-driven: you can configure fallbacks by error class (timeout, runtime error, OOM) and by percentiles (if latency > SLO for N requests). fallback order is model variant compatibility aware — we won't fall back from a model using tools/functions to a variant that lacks tool support.
02:32 Ethan: and where is the KV cache hit info? we observed big variance in token times earlier.
02:40 Lina: right, on the inspector you can expand the model exec span and see cache stats: kv_cache_hit=3, kv_cache_miss=12, prefix_cache_hit_ratio=0.2. those are estimated from the serving runtime telemetry.
02:53 Priya: those numbers — are they sampled or full fidelity? we need per-request deterministic counts for debugging.
03:02 Omar: we keep per-request KV deltas in the trace but for long-running logs we sample. for the pilot we can enable full fidelity for your request set — note that'll increase telemetry ingestion costs.
03:18 Sana: can you show the correlation to infra logs? e.g., which GPU and which pod was involved?
03:24 Lina: sure, clicking the infra link. here we correlate request id to node id gtx-03a, pod redwood-serving-77f, container pid 4921. below that there's a link to the node-level syslog and to GPU utilization metrics.
03:40 Markus: perfect. so if we see OOMs can we map to the exact model size and sequence length distribution?
03:48 Lina: yes, the exec span includes model_version, seq_len, allocated_mem_mb, and whether quantized kernels were used. note: model_version strings sometimes get truncated in ASR so watch for typos in the transcript.
03:59 Jordan: haha noted. also important — when we capture allocated_mem_mb it's approximate on shared nodes due to other tenant workloads in Hosted mode; in Dedicated it's per-pod exact.
04:15 Priya: about security — Ethan, do you want us to pause so you can ask about KMS and audit logs?
04:22 Ethan: yes please, short. our compliance team requires customer-managed KMS and immutable audit trails for any production inference. do you support HSM and long retention?
04:33 Jordan: yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and we can route audit logs to your SIEM or to an S3 in your VPC with immutability flags. we'll attach the SOC2 package in the follow-up.
04:47 Ethan: also need SAML SSO and RBAC for the console.
04:52 Omar: supported — SSO via SAML/OIDC and fine grained RBAC. console actions like model promote/rollback are gated.
05:01 Priya: back to the failure flow — you showed a retry with a smaller model. how do you ensure semantic continuity? our product needs consistent outputs, not sudden regressions when fallback occurs.
05:12 Lina: we have similarity and output-quality checks as part of the fallback policy. you can set a quality threshold: if the fallback output drifts beyond X% from the canonical, we'll mark the request as degraded but not automatically return it to the user; you can configure to degrade gracefully or to return the original error.
05:30 Markus: hmm interesting. what's the tooling for testing drift?
05:34 Lina: in Optimize we run evals on your prompt set across candidate fallbacks and surface a delta score. we can attach per-prompt diffs in the trace metadata during the pilot.
05:44 Jordan: ok now i'll simulate a real failure chain — lina, can you force a kernel OOM for that pod?
05:51 Lina: doing it now... (background typing) — triggering synthetic OOM. you'll see an error span appear in the timeline.
06:10 Lina: there — error span popped: internal runtime error: kernel out of memory. the trace shows a 500-level error upstream and then a fallback attempt. expanding the error shows stack snippets and the container stderr. note: sensitive environment variables are redacted in the console view.
06:28 Priya: container stderr has a weird unicode token in the stack trace — is that ASR or actual log content?
06:34 Lina: likely actual log content. useful tidbit: when we ingest logs we sanitize and then optionally keep raw logs in your VPC for audits.
06:44 Marcus: (interrupting) Markus: sorry, small typo — when you said 'Marcus' earlier it's Markus.
06:49 Jordan: thanks — flagged for the transcript.
06:54 Sana: about alerting — can we get notified when fallbacks exceed 1% of requests?
07:00 Omar: yep, alerts can be dimensioned by model, route, or tenant. we can push to PagerDuty, Slack, or your webhook.
07:08 Priya: will alerts include the trace link so SREs can jump straight to the console?
07:12 Lina: yes the alert payload includes trace url, request id, and a brief top-level diagnostic.
07:20 Markus: curious about sampling: you mentioned full fidelity for pilot. what's the retention window for traces and how much egress will that add?
07:29 Jordan: default retention 30 days for traces in Hosted; enterprise plans can extend to 90/365 with cold storage in your S3. in Private, retention is controlled by you. egress depends on fidelity, but our pilot estimate sheet will show sample sizes and cost.
07:45 Priya: can we get a CSV export of traces for offline analysis?
07:49 Lina: yes, export includes spans, timings, cache metrics, and any linked infra ids; we also provide a parquet export for large workloads.
07:58 Ethan: security follow-up: will traces include PII? we need automated redaction.
08:04 Jordan: we support redaction rules at ingestion — regex-based and schema-based PII scrubbing. we can also run a redaction job during export. we'll include recommended rules in the security pack.
08:17 Sana: show us a real-world RPS spike scenario please — how does the console show congestion and backpressure?
08:24 Lina: switching to a flood test trace. here you see queue length rising, request latency percentiles spike, and fallback policies kicking in. the timeline view has a heatmap for queue wait times per node.
08:38 Lina: you can also toggle the routing policy view to see requests routed by latency vs cost — we use smart routing. in this test we prioritized latency and it pushed extra load to Dedicated pool.
08:50 Markus: what's the recommended approach for hybrid workloads where some PII must stay on-prem?
08:56 Omar: route PII requests to your Private/On-Prem endpoints via request tags. the console shows route metadata and enforces policy-level routing. we also provide an SDK flag to annotate PII at request time.
09:10 Priya: last thing — for the pilot, we'll want the SE to run our 5k token set and see end-to-end behaviour and cost delta between Hosted/Dedicated. can Lina do that?
09:19 Lina: yes — i'll run it in a sandbox Dedicated pool for exact metrics.
09:24 Jordan: great. i'll send over the pilot template and SOC2 docs after this call. any other questions?
09:30 Markus: none from me. thanks for the depth — this is promising.
09:33 Ethan: one more — can you show where the audit trail records manual rollbacks?
09:38 Lina: yes, clicking account audit logs — action show: model.promote v1.12 -> v1.13 by Jordan.patel at 14:03, ip masked. it's immutable and exportable.
09:50 Sana: perfect.
09:52 Jordan: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps in chat and we'll sync on pilot kickoff.
09:58 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had issues with a few proper names and some kernel-level log snippets; manual timestamps approximate.
